Severe thunderstorm winds blew large limbs off trees and knocked down trees northeast of Gonzales.
A tornado touched down twice near SH97. It destroyed some chicken houses. The tornado was rated EF0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.
A manager of a travel stop along I-10 reported one inch hail.
A six to seven foot long piece of sheet metal was torn from a business' car canopy.
Public reported tree limbs being blown down.
Numerous power lines and trees down in Nixon.
Dime and nickel size hail was reported at the intersection of US Hwy 87 and FM108 in Smiley.
An employee at Mouton Feed Company reported penny size hail northwest of Mouton.
Thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 50 knots, knocked down a tree across the road leading into the Palmetto State Park.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 knots that damaged four large barns, downed several 18 inch diameter trees, and blew a metal windmill onto a tractor.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 50 mph which knocked down large tree limbs along FM 1682.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to two inches in diameter which damaged several cars.

Strong thunderstorm winds, estimated at 50 mph, blew down several trees, large limbs, and produced roof damage on several buildings and homes. The damage was mainly found a few blocks either side of Highway 90 and east of Highway 97 near Waelder.
